libraries.name: Quick_digital_IO_interrupt
libraries.author: 埃博拉酱 <vhtmfu@outlook.com>
libraries.sentence: 高性能引脚IO和中断操作。**非兼容性更新，谨慎升级**
libraries.paragraph: 内置的引脚读写函数`digitalRead`和`digitalWrite`需要每次将引脚转换成寄存器地址再进行读写，而且还需要检查PWM计时器设定，虽然增加了可靠性，减少了内存占用，但是性能较低，无法满足超高频操作的需求。内置的引脚中断操作功能也十分有限。本库牺牲一定内存空间和与其它功能的兼容性和稳健性，追求使用尽可能少的指令周期完成引脚操作，并支持内置函数所欠缺的一些扩展功能。

libraries.sentence: Validated RC receiver mapping for Arduino with iBUS, ESP32 SBUS, shaping, filtering, and failsafe handling.

libraries.name: EEProm_Safe_Wear_Level
libraries.author: Torsten Frieser / automatician
libraries.sentence: Robust EEPROM Wear-Leveling with CRC, Lifetime Override and Audit Functions.
libraries.paragraph: A specialized library for Arduino EEPROM ensuring CRC long-term data integrity and providing explicit control over wear-leveling cycles. Meets the high requirements for robustness and failure safety needed in commercial or critical projects: Detection of data corruption / security within the EEPROM itself. Prevention of overwriting program memory in case of faulty application. Securing control data structures (RAM Handle Structure) against corruption (overwriting / data modification). CRC checksums with an increased detection rate.

libraries.name: SuperCANBus
libraries.author: Juan Pablo Risso <juano23@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A modern, robust communication protocol for the age of AI. Enhanced Arduino CAN Bus library with pub/sub protocol, persistent IDs, automatic subscription restoration, and extended frame support.
libraries.paragraph: Supports Microchip MCP2515 based boards/shields and the Espressif ESP32's built-in SJA1000 compatible CAN controller. Features complete broker-client architecture with topic-based messaging, sequential client ID assignment (1, 2, 3...), persistent ID registration with serial numbers, automatic subscription restoration after power cycles, extended CAN frames for messages >8 bytes, flash memory persistence (ESP32 NVS/Arduino EEPROM), and event-driven callbacks. Client mappings and subscriptions survive power cycles.

libraries.paragraph: The AlashIRControl library, developed by Айтен Бексултан from Alash-electronics.kz, provides a robust solution for working with infrared (IR) transmitters and receivers using Arduino. Comprehensive examples and protocols make it easy to implement and customize for various applications, enhancing your IR-based projects' capabilities.

libraries.sentence: Arduino library for the STMicroelectronics LIS2DH12 accelerometer.
libraries.paragraph: The LIS2DH12 is an ultra-low-power high-performance three-axis linear accelerometer belonging to the femto family with digital I2C/SPI serial interface standard output. The LIS2DH12 has user-selectable full scales of ±2g/±4g/±8g/±16g and is capable of measuring accelerations with output data rates from 1 Hz to 5.3 kHz. The device may be configured to generate interrupt signals by detecting two independent inertial wake-up/free-fall events as well as by the position of the device itself.

libraries.name: InstantIoT
libraries.author: JeanLoick DT <jeanloickdt@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Arduino client for the InstantIoT mobile app — bridges ESP32, ESP8266 and Arduino Uno R4 WiFi with a simple declarative DSL.
libraries.paragraph: Connects your Arduino board to the InstantIoT mobile app over Wi-Fi. Two active transports: Wi-Fi SoftAP (the board hosts its own Wi-Fi, no router) and Wi-Fi client to a self-hosted InstantIoT Server (multi-device, with history). Seventeen widgets out of the box: simple/advanced/emergency buttons, horizontal/vertical sliders, switch, joystick, direction pad, segmented switch, LED, gauge, metric, bar chart, advanced chart, horizontal/vertical level meters and text. Declarative DSL: file-scope blocks like ISimpleButton("btn1") { WHEN_PRESSED { ... } } — no boilerplate. Compact binary protocol about 5x smaller than JSON. Bluetooth Classic, BLE and SoftwareSerial transports ship in source as preview — they are not currently exposed by the mobile app (see README).

libraries.name: InstantIoT
libraries.author: JeanLoick DT <jeanloickdt@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Arduino client for the InstantIoT mobile app — the board writes a value at an address, the app decides what it looks like.
libraries.paragraph: Connects an ESP32, ESP8266 or Arduino Uno R4 WiFi to the InstantIoT mobile app — over the board's own Wi-Fi, through a server you host, or through the InstantIoT Cloud over TLS. One header, one object, one begin(): InstantIoT.begin(WiFiLink(ssid, pass), Cloud(token)). The board writes values at addresses I0..I255 and reacts to the ones written to it; whether a value is drawn as a gauge, a chart or a number is decided in the app, without reflashing. Declarative DSL at file scope: ISimpleButton(I0) { WHEN_PRESSED { ... } } and ISignal(I5, float setpoint) { ... } — no boilerplate. A setpoint survives a reboot: the server replays it on connect. Compact binary protocol, 14 bytes for a float, no dynamic memory. Bluetooth Classic, BLE and SoftwareSerial links ship in source as preview — the mobile app does not expose them yet (see README).

libraries.paragraph: It packages the necessary functions for using it as an ad-hoc network: group settings, role settings, security settings, automatic peer pairing via broadcasting, and status monitoring of connected peers via heartbeat. This makes wireless communication in ESP32 environments—previously expensive and complex—simple and affordable.

libraries.name: RoboServo
libraries.author: dunknowcoding
libraries.sentence: A high-performance servo control library for ESP32 family and ESP8266 with multi-servo support.
libraries.paragraph: RoboServo provides easy-to-use functions for controlling multiple servos on ESP32 variants (ESP32, ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3, ESP32-C3, ESP32-C6, ESP32-H2, ESP32-P4) and ESP8266. libraries.name: BLEOTA
libraries.author: gb88
libraries.sentence: Perform OTA updates on ESP32 over BLE.
libraries.paragraph: OTA firmware and filesystem updates over BLE for every ESP32 variant. On arduino-esp32 core 3.3.0+ the library uses the core's BLEDevice.h and works on every chip (BlueDroid on classic ESP32, NimBLE on S3/C3/C6/H2) without requiring NimBLE-Arduino and without link conflicts. On older cores (2.x, 3.0-3.2) the library keeps the legacy dual-backend behaviour: NimBLE-Arduino is used if installed, otherwise BlueDroid. The NimBLE-Arduino examples in examples/nimble/ are only supported on core <3.3.0. Supports sector CRC-16, zlib compression and optional RSA-2048 signature verification.

libraries.name: BuzzerPIO_RP2040
libraries.author: Ângelo
libraries.sentence: Zero-jitter tone generation for passive buzzers using the RP2040 PIO coprocessor.
libraries.paragraph: Generates square waves entirely in hardware via a PIO state machine. Features hardware-timed melody sequencing (alarm chain), volume control through instruction patching, and a non-blocking API. No CPU polling, no PWM conflicts, no tone() blocking. Supports frequencies from 15 Hz to 976 kHz.

libraries.name: BuzzerPIO_RP2040
libraries.author: Ângelo Moisés Alves
libraries.sentence: Ultrasonic PWM tone generation for passive buzzers using the RP2040 PIO coprocessor.
libraries.paragraph: Dual state-machine architecture: SM1 generates an ultrasonic PWM carrier (~95 kHz) for distortion-free volume control, SM2 gates it at the audible frequency. Uses only 4 PIO instructions, auto-probes both PIO blocks, zero DMA, zero IRQ handlers. Coexists with OneWirePIO, DHT22PIO, and CYW43 WiFi. Non-blocking melody sequencing via hardware alarm chain. Drop-in replacement for v1.x.

libraries.name: BuzzerPIO_RP2040

libraries.paragraph: Dual state-machine architecture: SM1 generates an ultrasonic PWM carrier (~95 kHz) for distortion-free volume control, SM2 gates it at the audible frequency. Uses only 4 PIO instructions, auto-probes both PIO blocks, zero DMA, zero IRQ handlers. Multi-core safe via hardware spinlock. Coexists with OneWirePIO, DHT22PIO, and CYW43 WiFi. Non-blocking melody sequencing via hardware alarm chain with completion callback. Pause/resume support. Perceptually linear volume curve. Drop-in replacement for v1.x/v2.x.

libraries.sentence: Buehlmann ZHL-16C decompression model for DIY dive computer
libraries.paragraph: Scuba diving decompression calculations using Buehlmann ZHL-16C algorithm with gradient factor

libraries.name: OSynaptic-RX
libraries.author: OpenSynaptic Contributors
libraries.sentence: OpenSynaptic RX-only packet decoder for 8-bit MCUs (pure C89).
libraries.paragraph: Decodes incoming OpenSynaptic wire packets (FULL format) into sensor readings with CRC validation. No transmit or encode path included. Minimal RAM footprint; no dynamic allocation; integer-only arithmetic (no float required). Compatible with OpenSynaptic Python hubs and OSynaptic-TX sensor nodes.

libraries.name: OSynaptic-TX
libraries.author: OSynaptic-TX Maintainers
libraries.sentence: Lightweight TX-only packet encoder for 8-bit MCUs (pure C89, no heap).
libraries.paragraph: Encodes sensor readings into OpenSynaptic wire packets. Three API tiers: dynamic, compile-time static, and zero-buffer streaming. No receive or decode path included. Compatible with OpenSynaptic server and OSynaptic-FX gateway.

libraries.name: DIYables LCD I2C
libraries.author: DIYables.io
libraries.sentence: The Arduino library for controlling I2C LCD displays (16x2, 20x4) with helper functions, custom characters, and multiple I2C bus support. Compatible with Arduino, ESP32, ESP8266, STM32, Raspberry Pi Pico, and more.
libraries.paragraph: This library is designed for HD44780-based I2C LCD displays. It provides LiquidCrystal-compatible API plus helper functions (text alignment, progress bars, predefined custom characters). Supports multiple I2C buses (Wire, Wire1, Wire2) for advanced boards like Arduino Giga, Due, and ESP32. Compatible with all Arduino-based platforms including Arduino Uno, Mega, Nano, ESP32, ESP8266, STM32, and Raspberry Pi Pico.

libraries.name: 7Semi BMP384
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Lightweight and efficient BMP384 pressure and temperature sensor library.
libraries.paragraph: Provides a clean, high-performance interface for Bosch BMP384 sensors over I2C and SPI. Includes support for FIFO, interrupts, filtering, oversampling, and altitude calculation. Designed for embedded efficiency and ease of use.

libraries.name: 7Semi MLX90393
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: MLX90393 3-axis magnetometer library
libraries.paragraph: Lightweight and configurable Arduino library for the MLX90393 sensor. Supports magnetic field measurement (µT), configurable gain, resolution, OSR, filter, and ESP32 custom I2C pins.

libraries.name: 7Semi-TMP102
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for the TMP102 digital temperature sensor.
libraries.paragraph: Arduino driver for the Texas Instruments TMP102 I2C digital temperature sensor supporting temperature measurement, alert configuration, conversion rate control, and power saving modes.

libraries.name: 7Semi DAC7578
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Arduino driver for Texas Instruments DAC7578 8-channel 12-bit I2C DAC.
libraries.paragraph: Lightweight production-grade driver for the TI DAC7578. Supports voltage and raw DAC writes, synchronous channel updates, LDAC register control, clear code register, and power-down modes. Includes internal channel caching for fast readback.

libraries.name: 7Semi_BME68x
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for Bosch BME68x environmental sensor with I2C and SPI support.
libraries.paragraph: Provides temperature, humidity, pressure and gas resistance readings from the Bosch BME68x sensor. Supports I2C and SPI communication, heater configuration, sampling control and multiple heater profiles.

libraries.name: 7Semi BMP58x
libraries.author: 7Semi <info@7semi.com>
libraries.sentence: Lightweight BMP58x driver for Arduino (I2C/SPI) with beginner-friendly defaults.
libraries.paragraph: Arduino library for the Bosch Sensortec BMP58x barometric pressure sensor. Supports I2C and SPI on Arduino-core boards (ESP32/AVR/STM32/RP2040 etc). Includes safe default configuration via initSensor() so the sensor works out-of-box, plus helpers for OSR/ODR/IIR, interrupts, FIFO, OOR window, and NVM access. Optional I2C/SPI pin mapping is supported on ESP32 cores.

libraries.name: 7Semi VEML7700
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for the VEML7700 ambient light sensor.
libraries.paragraph: This library provides an easy interface for the Vishay VEML7700 ambient light sensor. It supports lux measurement, white channel reading, interrupt configuration, power saving modes, and automatic gain/integration adjustment for accurate measurements across a wide light range.

libraries.name: 7Semi_MAX31856
libraries.author: 7Semi <info@7semi.com>
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for MAX31856 thermocouple amplifier.
libraries.paragraph: This library provides an easy interface to the MAX31856 thermocouple-to-digital converter. It supports thermocouple configuration, temperature reading, fault detection, and threshold configuration.

libraries.name: 7Semi STS3x
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for the Sensirion STS3x digital temperature sensor.
libraries.paragraph: Provides an easy-to-use interface for the Sensirion STS3x temperature sensor over I2C. Supports single-shot and periodic measurements with CRC validation and configurable repeatability levels.

libraries.name: 7Semi_TMAG5273
libraries.author: 7Semi <info@7semi.com>
libraries.sentence: Arduino driver for Texas Instruments TMAG5273 3-axis Hall-effect magnetic sensor.
libraries.paragraph: Arduino library for the TMAG5273 magnetic sensor including magnetic field measurement, temperature sensing, angle calculation, threshold detection, interrupts, configurable averaging and power modes.

libraries.name: 7Semi ENS210
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: ENS210 temperature and humidity sensor library for Arduino.
libraries.paragraph: High-accuracy ENS210 temperature and humidity sensor library with CRC validation, single-shot and continuous modes, and Kelvin/Celsius/Fahrenheit/Absolute humidity calculations. Optimized for ESP32, AVR, and other Arduino-compatible platforms.

libraries.name: 7Semi STS4x
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for Sensirion STS4x digital temperature sensors over I2C.
libraries.paragraph: Lightweight and easy-to-use Arduino library for Sensirion STS4x temperature sensors. Supports single-shot measurements, CRC validation for data integrity, configurable repeatability (precision levels), and optional smoothing filter. Designed for Arduino, ESP32, and other I2C-compatible platforms.

libraries.name: RapidBootWiFi
libraries.author: Idlan Zafran Mohd Zaidie
libraries.sentence: Handles 3-rapid-boot WiFi resets, LittleFS boot counting, and WiFiManager setup.
libraries.paragraph: A robust, drop-in library for ESP32 and ESP8266 devices that automatically handles WiFi provisioning via a Captive Portal, and provides a physical "Factory Reset" mechanism by power-cycling the device 3 times rapidly. Includes flash-memory parameter auto-saving and non-blocking background reconnects.

libraries.name: SerialCommandCoordinator

libraries.sentence: A memory-efficient, zero-heap, non-blocking serial command dispatcher.

Features include automatic buffer overflow recovery, in-place parameter extraction, interactive sub-mode polling, and seamless compatibility across 8-bit and 32-bit Arduino architectures.

libraries.name: AdvancedCLI
libraries.author: Maximiliano Ramirez <maximiliano.ramirezbravo@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: A serial CLI for Arduino: register commands, parse arguments, and receive typed callbacks with zero-heap allocation.
libraries.paragraph: AdvancedCLI turns the Serial Monitor into a full command-line interface. Define commands with named arguments, boolean flags, integers, floats, positional values, sub-commands, and aliases. Callbacks receive strongly-typed parsed values, help output is generated automatically, and optional validation and error hooks keep the interface robust. No dynamic allocation, fixed-size buffers, compatible with AVR and 32-bit architectures.

libraries.name: KISS_FFT
libraries.author: Meer Zafarullah Noohani <https://github.com/meerzafarnoohani>
libraries.sentence: A lightweight mixed-radix FFT library for Arduino and ESP32.
libraries.paragraph: KISS FFT (Keep It Simple, Stupid) converts time-domain signals into the frequency domain, enabling audio analysis, vibration sensing, pitch detection, and real-time spectrum visualization. This Arduino port wraps the original C library by Mark Borgerding with a clean C++ class, built-in windowing (Hann, Hamming), magnitude spectrum output, dominant frequency detection, and I2S microphone support for ESP32.

libraries.name: ETL_Arduino
libraries.author: Meer Zafarullah Noohani <https://github.com/meerzafarnoohani>
libraries.sentence: Embedded Template Library (ETL). Fixed size containers and state machines for Arduino and ESP32 with zero heap allocation.
libraries.paragraph: ETL_Arduino provides production-grade, no-heap C++ containers for embedded systems: fixed-size vector, queue (circular buffer), map (key-value store), string, and a finite state machine with enter/exit/update callbacks. Designed as a safe replacement for STL on Arduino and ESP32 where heap fragmentation is a concern. All storage is compile-time allocated, no malloc, no new, no fragmentation.

libraries.name: PulseWetProbe
libraries.author: Parvaz Jamei
libraries.sentence: MCU-only pulsed electrode wetness, soil moisture, conductivity trend, and surface-state sensing.
libraries.paragraph: PulseWetProbe is an Arduino library for MCU-only two-plate electrode sensing. It supports high/low pulsed drive, reversible two-plate role swapping, dry/wet and multi-point calibration, board-aware defaults, analogReadResolution-aware normalization, guarded ESP32 touch sensing when available, fixed-memory noise filtering, pro diagnostics, CSV output, optional JSON outside tiny mode, power-aware sampling, and anti-corrosion Hi-Z rest behavior. It does not claim certified EC, salinity, freezing-point, or RWIS accuracy.

Supports unicast and broadcast text commands with automatic fragmentation for long commands (e.g. saving large stored sequences), raw binary forwarding for Pololu/Maestro servo packets via WCBStream, ETM heartbeat and ACK tracking, board online/offline status callbacks, and communication with an out-of-band special peer such as NaviCore via enableSpecialPeer(). A raw-packet hook (onRawPacket/sendRawPacket) lets custom protocols — such as firmware OTA — ride the same ESP-NOW mesh. setIdentity() advertises the device over WDP so WCBs discover it by name and firmware version automatically (the mesh twin of the serial WDP-DA device-announce model), setPortLabel() advertises this device's own per-serial-port labels (the WDP PORTLABEL TLV) so the Wizard and WCBs show what is attached to each of its ports, setMaestroIds() advertises the Maestro controllers this device hosts (the WDP MAESTRO and MAESTRO_CFG TLVs) so WCBs learn where they live and can route to them, and onNeighbor()/getNeighbor() consume the same WDP adverts to learn every WCB and client on the mesh — alias, firmware, capabilities, controller link and Maestro IDs. With auto-join (on by default) the device also registers regular WCBs it hears as ESP-NOW peers live and remembers them across reboots, so it discovers the fleet once and never needs wcb_quantity to cover it. A bulk-transfer facility (onBulkBegin/onBulkChunk/onBulkComplete) streams payloads too large to hold in RAM to consumer-owned storage with a selective-NACK back-channel, and inbound COMMANDs are de-duplicated by sequence number.

libraries.name: NeuDB
libraries.author: Ulywae <ulywae@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: An industrial-grade, ultra-lean LSM-Tree storage engine with power-fail safety for ESP32.
libraries.paragraph: NeuDB (NeuLSMDB_FS) is a high-performance, asynchronous Log-Structured Merge-tree storage engine tailored for write-heavy embedded logging. Utilizing a FreeRTOS background compaction scheduler, integrated Bloom Filters, and Binary Search (std::lower_bound), it reduces storage write amplification and slashes read latencies down to microseconds. Features atomic Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) for bulletproof crash recovery against sudden power failures on Flash memory (LittleFS).

libraries.sentence: Ultra-lean, transactional Twin-Engine LSM-Tree storage engine with power-fail resilient lifecycle protection for ESP32.
libraries.paragraph: NeuDB v2.0.0 Asynchronous Log-Structured Merge-tree storage engine tailored for write-heavy embedded logging and circular telemetry tracking. Utilizing an isolated FreeRTOS background compaction scheduler on CPU Core 1, real-time adaptive dynamic boundary monitors, integrated hardware-backed Bloom Filters, and binary index lookaheads, it minimizes flash write amplification and slashes read latencies down to microseconds. Features atomic Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) packed with hardware CRC32 for bulletproof cold crash recovery against sudden power sabotage.

libraries.name: LGFXVirtualCanvas
libraries.author: TANAKA Masayuki
libraries.sentence: Virtual full-screen canvas over LovyanGFX / M5GFX via vertical tiling.
libraries.paragraph: Draw to a virtual full-screen canvas even when a full double-buffer does not fit in RAM. The screen is split into vertical tiles rendered into a small reused sprite; your draw callback runs once per tile in virtual coordinates and the library hides the Y offset, clipping, and flush. Include your graphics library (LovyanGFX / M5GFX / M5Unified) before this header.

libraries.name: PotIO
libraries.author: Little Man Builds
libraries.sentence: Practical potentiometer and joystick input handling with calibration, deadzones, filtering, shaping, and slew limiting.
libraries.paragraph: Zero-allocation Arduino input library for LinearPot, Joystick2D, ContinuousPot, and SteppedPot. Includes generic analogRead support, ESP32-only millivolt/attenuation helpers, jitter-to-deadzone tools, compact factory builders, and SnapshotBus-friendly frames.

libraries.name: PotIO
libraries.author: Little Man Builds (Darren Osborne)
libraries.sentence: Reliable potentiometer and joystick inputs with explicit validity, calibration, shaping, filtering, and slew limiting.
libraries.paragraph: Zero-allocation Arduino input library for LinearPot, Joystick2D, ContinuousPot, and SteppedPot with explicit sample validity and errors, strict or permissive calibration, independent processing stages, timing-gap protection, joystick geometry policies, continuous-wrap plausibility checks, durable step-change sequencing, rolling jitter tools, generic readers, and ESP32 ADC helpers. PotIO owns signal conditioning rather than application safety policy and has no dependency on other LMB libraries. ESP32-S3 is the primary reference target; other listed architectures are compile-validation targets for the portable core.

libraries.name: SwitchBank
libraries.author: Little Man Builds (Darren Osborne)
libraries.sentence: Debounced N-bit switch bank with polarity, latch modes, snapshot, and edge masks.
libraries.paragraph: Header-only, Arduino-friendly library for DIP/slide/rocker banks (1..32 bits). Features per-bit debouncing, compile-time or runtime polarity, latch/clear-on-read flags, optional scan throttling, rising/falling edge masks, POD snapshot access, and an optional on-commit callback. Flexible reader callbacks support GPIO or expanders (e.g., MCP23017). Constructors/factories are side-effect free; call sync() once after IO init to establish a clean baseline (no edges on boot). Includes a beginner Arduino helper and expander examples.

libraries.author: Little Man Builds (Darren Osborne)

libraries.sentence: Library for the ProtoCentral TMF8829 multi-zone time-of-flight sensor breakout board.
libraries.paragraph: The TMF8829 is an ams-OSRAM direct time-of-flight (dToF) sensor with up to 48x32 zones, up to 11 m range and 0.25 mm resolution over I2C. This library handles the cold-boot bootloader handshake, streams the bundled ams-OSRAM RAM firmware into the chip, and decodes per-zone distance (mm) and confidence for all four focal-plane modes (8x8 / 16x16 / 32x32 / 48x32) with (x, y) accessors. Includes a ProtoCentral OpenView streaming example.

libraries.name: python esp bridge
libraries.author: Hamza Yesilmen <resmiyslmn@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Flash-once ESP32 firmware that exposes every peripheral to Python over USB serial or Bluetooth.
libraries.paragraph: Turns an ESP32 into a live bridge — GPIO, ADC/DAC, PWM, touch, I2C, SPI, UART, Wi-Fi sockets, BLE, ESP-NOW, RMT, 1-Wire, CAN, I2S, filesystem, NVS and OTA are all driven from the host with the python-esp-bridge package (pip install python-esp-bridge). One EspBridge.begin() call starts a FreeRTOS task model (separate TX, RX and network tasks) so blocking radio I/O never stalls peripheral traffic. Requires arduino-esp32 core 3.x.

libraries.name: NiusZigbee
libraries.author: dunknowcoding (NiusRobotLab)
libraries.sentence: Drive external Zigbee / IEEE 802.15.4 radio modules (CC2530, ...) from an ArduinoNRF nRF52840 board.
libraries.paragraph: Host-side drivers for external 2.4 GHz IEEE 802.15.4 modules over a hardware UART. Ships an SDCC transceiver firmware for the AliExpress CC2530 module plus a raw-802.15.4 API (send / receive / promiscuous sniff). Flash the module firmware with the ArduinoNRF board package's built-in CC-Debugger - no external TI programmer required. Extensible to more modules and a future Z-Stack (full Zigbee PRO) backend.

libraries.name: NiusZigbee
libraries.author: dunknowcoding (NiusRobotLab)
libraries.sentence: Drive external Zigbee / IEEE 802.15.4 radio modules (CC2530, ...) from an ArduinoNRF nRF52840 board.
libraries.paragraph: Host-side drivers for external 2.4 GHz IEEE 802.15.4 modules over a hardware UART. Ships an SDCC transceiver firmware for the AliExpress CC2530 module plus a raw-802.15.4 API (send / receive / promiscuous sniff). Flash the module firmware with the ArduinoNRF board package's built-in CC-Debugger - no external TI programmer required. Extensible to more modules and a future Z-Stack (full Zigbee PRO) backend.

libraries.name: NiusZigbee
libraries.author: dunknowcoding (NiusRobotLab)
libraries.sentence: Drive external Zigbee / IEEE 802.15.4 radio modules (CC2530, ...) from an ArduinoNRF nRF52840 board.
libraries.paragraph: Host-side Zigbee / IEEE 802.15.4 stack for external 2.4 GHz modules over a hardware UART. Ships an SDCC CC2530 MAC/PHY helper firmware (raw 802.15.4 send/receive, hardware PAN/address filtering, Auto ACK, CCA transmit, retries, promiscuous sniffing) and a growing native Zigbee PRO stack on the nRF52840: short-address MAC + association join, active scan + parent selection, AODV route discovery and multi-hop forwarding, AES-CCM* NWK and APS security, end-to-end acked delivery, APS fragmentation, ZDO discovery and network management (Mgmt_Lqi/Rtg), source binding, network-state persistence, Trust-Center key-transport tooling (AES-MMO/HMAC specialized keys), broadcast transaction table, sleepy-end-device queue + keep-alive, PAN-ID conflict frames, plus reusable Basic/OnOff cluster and reporting helpers. Flash the module firmware with the ArduinoNRF board package's built-in CC-Debugger - no external TI programmer required. Extensible to more modules and a future Z-Stack backend.

libraries.name: NiusZigbee
libraries.author: dunknowcoding (NiusRobotLab)
libraries.sentence: Drive external Zigbee / IEEE 802.15.4 radio modules (CC2530, ...) from an ArduinoNRF nRF52840 board.
libraries.paragraph: Host-side Zigbee / IEEE 802.15.4 stack for external 2.4 GHz modules over a hardware UART. Ships an SDCC CC2530 MAC/PHY helper firmware (raw 802.15.4 send/receive, hardware PAN/address filtering, Auto ACK, CCA transmit, retries, promiscuous sniffing) and a growing native Zigbee PRO stack on the nRF52840: short-address MAC + association join, active scan + parent selection, AODV route discovery and multi-hop forwarding, AES-CCM* NWK and APS security, end-to-end acked delivery, APS fragmentation, ZDO discovery and network management (Mgmt_Lqi/Rtg), source binding, network-state persistence, Trust-Center key-transport tooling (AES-MMO/HMAC specialized keys), broadcast transaction table, sleepy-end-device queue + keep-alive, PAN-ID conflict frames, plus reusable Basic/OnOff cluster and reporting helpers. Flash the module firmware with the ArduinoNRF board package's built-in CC-Debugger - no external TI programmer required. Extensible to more modules and a future Z-Stack backend.

libraries.paragraph: Host-side Zigbee / IEEE 802.15.4 stack for external 2.4 GHz modules over a hardware UART. Ships an SDCC CC2530 MAC/PHY helper firmware (raw 802.15.4 send/receive, hardware PAN/address filtering, Auto ACK, CCA transmit, retries, promiscuous sniffing) and a growing native Zigbee PRO stack on the nRF52840: short-address MAC + association join, active scan + parent selection, AODV route discovery and multi-hop forwarding, AES-CCM* NWK and APS security, end-to-end acked delivery, APS fragmentation, ZDO discovery and network management (Mgmt_Lqi/Rtg), source binding, network-state persistence, Trust-Center key-transport tooling (AES-MMO/HMAC specialized keys) with per-joiner install-code link keys and key rotation, broadcast transaction table, sleepy-end-device queue + keep-alive with the CC2530 v0.5 auto-ACK frame-pending bit, PAN-ID conflict + channel-change network manager, Touchlink + Green Power proxy/sink commissioning over real inter-PAN MAC frames, plus reusable ZCL device clusters and reporting helpers. Flash the module firmware with the ArduinoNRF board package's built-in CC-Debugger - no external TI programmer required. Extensible to more modules and a future Z-Stack backend.

libraries.name: NiusThread
libraries.author: dunknowcoding (NiusRobotLab)
libraries.sentence: Thread (OpenThread) IPv6 mesh networking on the ArduinoNRF nRF52840's native 2.4 GHz radio.
libraries.paragraph: A full OpenThread FTD stack (vendored, with mbedtls) running on a bare-metal IEEE 802.15.4 driver for the nRF52840's own RADIO peripheral - no SoftDevice, no external module, no nrfx. Form or join a Thread mesh with four calls (begin / setNetwork / start / process), then talk IPv6/UDP across it - or use the built-in CoAP layer (onCoapGet/onCoapPost/coapPost/coapGet) for resource-style control. The dataset and frame counters persist in flash, so nodes re-attach by themselves after a reboot. The complete official OpenThread C API stays available through Thread.instance(). Hardware-verified: two-node mesh (Leader + Child to Router), UDP multicast and CoAP LED control confirmed over the air, settings persistence across reset. Requires the ArduinoNRF board package.

libraries.name: NiusCrypto
libraries.author: NiusRobotLab
libraries.sentence: Hardware-accelerated cryptography for the ArduinoNRF board package, built on the nRF52840 CryptoCell 310 (CC310).
libraries.paragraph: One friendly API for random, hashing (SHA-256/HMAC), symmetric ciphers (AES-CBC/CTR/GCM) and public-key crypto (ECDSA / ECDH on P-256). It drives the real Arm CryptoCell 310 hardware accelerator through Nordic's CRYS runtime (libnrf_cc310.a) when vendored - SHA, AES-CBC/CTR, ECDSA/ECDH and the TRNG all run on hardware, with AES-GCM provided by nrf_oberon - and transparently falls back to the nRF52840 on-chip AES (ECB) and RNG peripherals plus a software SHA-256 when the blobs are absent. Pluggable backends mirror the ArduinoNRF-IMU bus design so the same sketch works either way. Import the CRYS binary with vendor/tools/import_cc310_sdk.py and fetch Oberon with vendor/tools/fetch_cc310.py --oberon-only; see docs/VENDORING.md and docs/BOARD_BRINGUP.md.

libraries.name: Fluxgrid

libraries.paragraph: Connect an ESP32 to your Fluxgrid dashboard in ~10 lines. libraries.name: ZenoPCB
libraries.author: ZENOPCB ELECTRONICS TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD <infor@zenopcb.vn>
libraries.sentence: Fluent IoT library for ESP32, ESP8266, UNO R4 WiFi and STM32 — WiFi provisioning, MQTT, OTA, Modbus, Z-Keys, alarms, schedules and irrigation.
libraries.paragraph: Single-entry-point library for the ZenoPCB IoT platform. Provides a fluent builder API (ZenoPCB::Zeno) for WiFi captive-portal provisioning, MQTT (with optional TLS), HTTP OTA with rollback, Modbus RTU/TCP with register-polling and MQTT control, Z-Key custom telemetry/control, edge alarm rules, schedule execution, irrigation scenarios, and diagnostics reporting. Optional features are gated by build flags: ZENOPCB_ENABLE_TLS, ZENOPCB_ENABLE_ETHERNET, ZENOPCB_ENABLE_CELLULAR.

Transport and codec logic stay in PCMFlowUDP and codec sibling libraries.

libraries.name: PCMFlowUDP
libraries.author: TANAKA Masayuki
libraries.sentence: UDP transport adapter for PCMFlow. Raw UDP, VBAN PCM, and RTP (PCMU / PCMA / G722 / L16 / Opus payload types) for streaming audio between Arduino devices and PCs.
libraries.paragraph: Plugs PCMFlow's PCMSource / PCMSink / ByteStream / ByteSink interfaces onto UDP. Provides RawUdpSink / RawUdpStream for caller-defined payloads, VbanSender / VbanReceiver for VB-Audio Voicemeeter and VBAN Receptor interop (PCM subset of VBAN), and RtpSender / RtpReceiver for VoIP / WebRTC interop via standard RFC 3550 / 3551 / 7587 payload types. Codes against the Arduino UDP base class, so it works with WiFiUDP on ESP32 and on the lang-ship:host test target. No third-party vendored code; MIT.

All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves RFC 7230 HTTP/1.1 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.paragraph: Serves HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (routes matched in insertion order; the parser validates every request byte-by-byte and auto-sends 400/413/414/501 with no application code), with HTTP/3 over QUIC in progress, plus WebSocket (RFC 6455), Server-Sent Events, Basic/Digest auth, static file serving, multipart, JSON, templating, and a middleware pipeline, plus opt-in HTTPS/TLS, SSH, Telnet, and SNMP (v1/v2c/v3). All buffers are statically sized at compile time and no heap is used after begin(); feature flags strip unused subsystems.

libraries.name: FOTA-Client-ESP32
libraries.author: NodeWave EA <info@nodewave.net>
libraries.sentence: Secure FOTA client for ESP32 with retry, lifecycle callbacks, SHA-256 and ECDSA/ED25519/RSA signature verification.
libraries.paragraph: Connects to a NodeWave FOTA platform backend to check for firmware updates, download and verify signed firmware (SHA-256 + ECDSA P-256 / ED25519 / RSA-SHA256 via mbedTLS), then flash via esp_https_ota. v1.0.0 adds: configurable retry with back-off (FOTA_RETRY_COUNT/DELAY), lifecycle event callback (onEvent), auto-fetch of signing public key (FOTA_AUTO_FETCH_PUBLIC_KEY), optional auto-reboot (FOTA_REBOOT_ON_SUCCESS), and per-library log-level control (FOTA_LOG_LEVEL). Supports campaign-aware OTA with live progress reporting.

Subclass LionTimerTask / LionShortTimerTask / LionCrudeTimerTask / LionCriticalTask and override TaskInnerBody(), or use LionSimpleTask to run a lambda without subclassing (ESP only). Critical tasks also run during Yield()/Delay(). Tasks register themselves by pointer and are non-copyable: create each once as a global/static or via new. Depends on LionArray. ESP8266 + AVR (on ESP32 use LionRtosTask instead).

libraries.name: LionTask
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Tiny cooperative (run-to-completion) task scheduler for ESP8266, ESP32 and AVR.
libraries.paragraph: Pump LionTask::Loop() from loop(); each task runs to completion on the main context (no preemption, no per-task stack). Subclass LionTimerTask / LionShortTimerTask / LionCrudeTimerTask / LionCriticalTask and override TaskInnerBody(), or use LionSimpleTask to run a lambda without subclassing (ESP only). Critical tasks also run during Yield()/Delay(). Tasks register themselves by pointer and are non-copyable: create each once as a global/static or via new. Depends on LionArray. ESP8266, ESP32 and AVR: on ESP32 real FreeRTOS tasks (LionRtosTask) are usually the better fit, but this scheduler is supported there and is the safe way to port a codebase that relies on single-threaded execution.

libraries.name: LionStreams
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Tiny Arduino Stream adapters: a String-backed stream and a chunk-flushing web-server stream.
libraries.paragraph: StringStream is a read/write Stream view over an external String (non-owning — the String must outlive the stream; reset() rewinds the read cursor and clears the String). ServerStream is a write-only Stream that buffers Print output and flushes it in chunks via server.sendContent() on ESP8266WebServer / ESP32 WebServer, so large HTML pages stream out without holding the whole response in RAM (start a chunked/unknown-length response first and call flush() at the end). Both are header-only and non-copyable. For ESPAsyncWebServer use the built-in beginResponseStream() instead.

libraries.name: LionDallas
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Compact DS18B20 driver over OneWire for the Lion* stack (ESP8266).
libraries.paragraph: Discovers DS18B20 addresses once at startup and keeps them (cures "the second sensor drops off"); reads them non-blocking inside a LionCriticalTask; caches the last good reading and rides out transient -127/fault values for a tolerance window. Includes the DallasTemperature 4.0.6 power-on-reset / insufficient-power / fault detection. Optional fixed addresses skip the unreliable SearchROM on long wiring (read by MatchROM). DS18B20 family (0x28) only. The consumer defines one global LionLogger Logger and pumps LionTask::Loop() from loop(). Portions ported from the Arduino Temperature Control Library (c) Miles Burton, MIT. ESP8266 only (on ESP32 there is no LionCriticalTask).

libraries.name: LionFastLcd
libraries.author: leva <leva.the.lion@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Change-tracked, buffered character-LCD layer over LiquidCrystal_I2C.
libraries.paragraph: Keeps a RAM shadow of the display and pushes only the cells that actually changed, coalescing runs of consecutive cells into a single setCursor() to cut I2C traffic. Implements Arduino Print, so use print()/println() as usual. Supports stacked/overlay screens via Clone()/Activate()/Deactivate() with a z-order. The class is non-copyable and objects are created only through CreateMain()/Clone() (they register in a static list and are meant to live for the program's lifetime); call CreateMain() once before any Clone()/Activate(). The shadow buffer is cols*rows bytes. Depends on LionArray and marcoschwartz/LiquidCrystal_I2C. Optional scrolling of over-long lines is ESP8266-only and OFF by default: build with -DFLCD_LONG_MESSAGES and add leva/LionTask. ESP8266 + AVR.

libraries.name: MicroTaskX
libraries.author: Moaaz Yahia Shrif
libraries.sentence: A modular micro-RTOS for Arduino with priority scheduling, task args, micros-precision timing, WDT, ISR queuing, coroutines, signals, mutexes, PID, Kalman, software PWM, rotary encoder, and rich hardware utilities.
libraries.paragraph: MicroTaskX v3.1 transforms Arduino into a high-efficiency micro-RTOS. Features: template-based priority scheduler with task arguments and microsecond precision, dynamic task management (add/remove/pause/resume/setInterval), one-shot tasks, task execution profiling, software watchdog timer (WDT), deferred ISR task queuing, cooperative coroutines and protothreads, inter-task signals and mutexes, real-time CPU usage monitoring, smart low-power sleep (AVR/ESP32), macro timers (MTX_EVERY_MS/HZ), EMA and moving-average analog smoothing, Kalman filter, software PWM, rotary encoder, PID controller with anti-windup, hysteresis logic, edge detection, long-press debouncing, battery percentage estimation, CRC8 checksum, time formatting, hex encoding, bit manipulation, LCD smart refresh, typewriter effect, and circular queue.

libraries.name: MicroTaskX
libraries.author: Moaaz Yahia Shrif
libraries.sentence: A modular micro-RTOS for Arduino with priority scheduling, task args, micros-precision timing, WDT, ISR queuing, coroutines, signals, mutexes, PID, Kalman, software PWM, rotary encoder, and real-time CPU profiling.
libraries.paragraph: MicroTaskX v3.1 transforms Arduino into a high-efficiency micro-RTOS. Features: template-based priority scheduler with task arguments and microsecond precision, dynamic task management (add/remove/pause/resume tasks at runtime), Watchdog Timer integration, ISR event queuing, cooperative coroutines, inter-task signals and mutexes, PID control, Kalman filtering, software PWM generation, rotary encoder support, and real-time CPU usage profiling. Includes smart low-power modes (Idle Sleep for AVR, Light Sleep for ESP32), hardware utilities for fast GPIO manipulation, analog smoothing with EMA filters, button debouncing, and independent macro timers. Zero-copy architecture maximizes performance on resource-constrained microcontrollers.

libraries.name: WcbCmd
libraries.author: Greg Hulette
libraries.sentence: Shared WCB command translators (device command -> native wire bytes).
libraries.paragraph: One command vocabulary for the whole WCB (Wireless Communication Board) ecosystem. Turns the WCB ";"-command verbs (;M Maestro, ;A MP3, ;L WLED, ;H HCR) into each device's native serial wire protocol, identically on any board. Compiled by BOTH the WCB firmware and a WCB_Client host (e.g. NaviCore) so the SAME command produces the SAME device bytes whether it is reached across the mesh over ESP-NOW (a WCB parses it) or out a host-local serial port (the host parses it). The library is pure translation (verb/action -> native bytes on an injected Stream); all routing, config, NVS and ESP-NOW relay stay in the firmware. Ships the Maestro (;M), MP3 (;A), WLED (;L) and HCR (;H) modules.

Compiled by BOTH the WCB firmware and a WCB_Client host (e.g. NaviCore) so the SAME command produces the SAME device bytes whether it is reached across the mesh over ESP-NOW (a WCB parses it) or out a host-local serial port (the host parses it). The library is pure translation (verb/action -> native bytes on an injected Stream); all routing, config, NVS and ESP-NOW relay stay in the firmware. Ships the Maestro (;M), MP3 (;A), WLED (;L) and HCR (;H) modules.

libraries.name: TameModbus
libraries.author: Ranindram Dutta
libraries.sentence: Minimal Modbus RTU master with a tunable, non-blocking response wait.
libraries.paragraph: Lightweight, dependency-free Modbus RTU master for reading holding registers over RS-232/RS-485. libraries.name: ModbusResponder
libraries.author: Levi Monte
libraries.sentence: Minimal Modbus TCP responder that serves holding registers to a PLC or SCADA master.
libraries.paragraph: A tiny, dependency-free implementation of Read Holding Registers (Modbus function code 0x03) over TCP, built directly against the Modbus Application Protocol spec. It is header-only and agnostic about where register values come from, making it well suited to resource-constrained boards where a full Modbus library's RAM and flash overhead is not justified for a single function code. Works with any Ethernet or WiFi transport that exposes the Arduino Client interface.

libraries.name: NessoLink
libraries.author: Ugur Sayar <ugursayar@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Versioned binary control-link protocol for the Nesso N1 robot controller.
libraries.paragraph: RemoteFrame v1/v2 codec (motors, up to two aux sticks, a 16-button bitfield, CRC-8 checked) plus WiFi UDP, TCP, BLE and LoRa (RadioLib) transports. The codec is header-only and dependency-free, so it runs on both the transmitter and the robot receiver on any board; each transport is compile-guarded, so codec-only users pull in no heavy dependencies.

libraries.name: UpdateOTW
libraries.author: Ítalo Coelho
libraries.sentence: Peer-to-peer firmware update over the wire (Modbus RTU / RS485).
libraries.paragraph: Stream a firmware image from a Modbus RTU master to a slave over a half-duplex RS485 bus, and the slave reboots into it. Two register-array state machines (UpdateOTW_Master sender, UpdateOTW_Slave receiver) — your code keeps doing the Modbus, the library only reads/writes a small register window. Non-blocking (one frame per tick), so the device keeps running while it updates, with deferred apply. Per-chunk CRC16 plus full-image CRC32, automatic retry with patient back-off, and free rollback via the ESP32 Update library. No external dependencies.

libraries.name: ESP32KeyBridge
libraries.author: TANAKA Masayuki
libraries.sentence: Bridge keyboard input to keyboard output on ESP32: remap, layers, macros, and layout conversion in between.
libraries.paragraph: ESP32KeyBridge sits between a keyboard and the machine that reads it. It takes input from USB Host keyboards, mice, gamepads and MIDI devices, BLE HID keyboards and mice, GPIO switches, key matrices and rotary encoders, normalizes it into one key model, merges several inputs into one, applies single-step remapping across key kinds, momentary layers, disabled keys, text macros and keyboard layout conversion, and writes the result to USB Device HID, BLE HID, or a serial Print. The core is portable C++ with no Arduino, ESP-IDF or hardware dependency; adapters are header-only, so a sketch needs EspUsbHost, EspUsbDevice or EspBle only for the adapters it includes.

The core is portable C++ with no Arduino, ESP-IDF or hardware dependency; adapters are header-only, so a sketch needs EspUsbHost, EspUsbDevice or EspBle only for the adapters it includes. libraries.name: MLBScoreboard
libraries.author: 5ne
libraries.sentence: Display live MLB scores on Inkplate e-paper boards (Inkplate 2 and larger).
libraries.paragraph: Fetches game data from the MLB Stats API into a simple struct, and separately ships Inkplate renderers to draw it: a compact single-game renderer for the tiny 3-color Inkplate 2, and a multi-game grid renderer for larger grayscale/color Inkplate boards. The data-fetching class (MLBScoreboard) handles WiFi, adaptive polling (slower pregame, fast during live games, stopped once final), and deep-sleep scheduling for battery-powered installs, and has no dependency on Inkplate or any display code -- pairing it with a renderer is left to your sketch.

libraries.name: ProtoCentral tinyGSR
libraries.author: ProtoCentral Electronics <support@protocentral.com>
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for the ProtoCentral tinyGSR electrodermal-activity (GSR/EDA) breakout - absolute skin conductance in microsiemens.
libraries.paragraph: Supports every tinyGSR revision from one library, selected at begin(). Drives the tinyGSR v2/v3 constant-voltage transimpedance front-end and reports ABSOLUTE skin conductance (microsiemens) and resistance, with an 8-tap smoothing filter, no-contact and over-range flags, and one-point self-calibration using the on-board Rcal resistor (JP1). Self-contained: drives the on-board 12-bit TLA2022 ADC (Lite tier) directly over I2C, no external ADC library required; an ADC-agnostic transfer-function helper supports the 16-bit ADS111x Standard tier. Qwiic / STEMMA QT. The original v1 board (LMV324 front-end, trimpot-set gain) is supported in relative ADC-count mode, replacing its dependency on the TLA20xx and FIR libraries.

libraries.sentence: Conecta un ESP32 a la plataforma IoT Tecnova por MQTT sobre WebSocket seguro (WSS).
libraries.paragraph: Maneja WiFi, la obtencion de credenciales via el webhook del dispositivo, la validacion TLS del broker, la reconexion automatica ante cortes, y el mapeo de variables del panel por nombre -- publicar un sensor o reaccionar a un comando queda reducido a un par de llamadas (setValue/onCommand), sin tocar MQTT ni certificados a mano. Los comandos del panel llegan a onCommand() con su tipo JSON: booleano para interruptores y botones, numero para deslizadores. Incluye manejo de consumo para proyectos a bateria: deepSleepSeconds() para sensores que solo publican, y enablePowerSave() para actuadores o dispositivos mixtos, que tienen que seguir alcanzables. Incluye tambien un modulo opcional (TecnovaProvisioning) para cargar las credenciales desde un portal cautivo en vez de escribirlas en el codigo.

libraries.name: TecnovaIoT
libraries.author: Tecnova
libraries.sentence: Conecta un ESP32 a la plataforma IoT Tecnova por MQTT sobre WebSocket seguro (WSS).

Los comandos del panel llegan a onCommand() con su tipo JSON: booleano para interruptores y botones, numero para deslizadores. Incluye manejo de consumo para proyectos a bateria: deepSleepSeconds() para sensores que solo publican, y enablePowerSave() para actuadores o dispositivos mixtos, que tienen que seguir alcanzables. Incluye tambien un modulo opcional (TecnovaProvisioning) para cargar las credenciales desde un portal cautivo en vez de escribirlas en el codigo. Incluye un modo sin reinicios (setAutoRestart(false)) para equipos con pantalla.

libraries.name: HomeAssistantDiscovery
libraries.author: Péter Soós
libraries.sentence: Home Assistant MQTT discovery payloads, built into caller-supplied buffers.
libraries.paragraph: Builds discovery topics and payloads from constexpr PROGMEM entity tables. No dynamic allocation, no JSON library, and no MQTT client — the application connects and publishes, so the same tables serve any client. Covers the single-state MQTT platforms (sensor, binary_sensor, button, number, select, switch); a publisher walks the tables and a matching clearer removes the retained messages again. Host-testable.

libraries.name: shark_pid
libraries.author: Tran Nguyen Binh <trannguyenbinh.shark@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Embedded 2-DOF PID controller that matches the Simulink PID Controller (2DOF) block.
libraries.paragraph: Every parameter maps one-to-one onto a field of the Simulink PID Controller (2DOF) block, so a model you tune in simulation is the controller that runs on the microcontroller - they agree to numerical noise even while the output is saturated. Explicit dt in every term so gains survive a change of loop rate. Setpoint weighting b and c, filter coefficient N, trapezoidal or backward-Euler integration, clamping and back-calculation anti-windup, integrator limits, NaN/Inf rejection and bumpless manual-to-auto transfer. The core has no Arduino or HAL dependency, so the same file builds for STM32, ESP-IDF or a PC simulation.

libraries.name: SNMP_Embedded
libraries.author: syntax <yard_botch.6g@icloud.com>
libraries.sentence: Memory-safe SNMPv2c agent with derived compile-time sizing.
libraries.paragraph: A full SNMPv2c agent: GET/GETNEXT/GETBULK/SET, v1/v2c TRAP and INFORM. Varbind cap and pool size are derived from the packet budget and your handler count (no magic numbers); the memory arena is locked in at boot so long-running nodes never fragment. Stateless trap/inform sends, loud tooBig rejection instead of silent drops, CI-validated (arduino-lint, host Catch2 suite, ESP8266+ESP32 example matrix).

libraries.name: FmtLog
libraries.author: Aleksey Grishin <g-iot@mail.ru>
libraries.sentence: Форматирование строк по образцу {} и лёгкий журнал для микроконтроллеров.
libraries.paragraph: Сообщение задаётся образцом, где место каждого значения помечено {} - текст виден целиком и не разорван знаками вставки. Без динамической памяти и без std::string: буфер задаётся снаружи и не растёт. Готовые правила вывода для чисел, строк во флеше и EEPROM, даты и времени, длительностей, IP-адресов и дампов памяти; свой тип подключается одной специализацией formatter<T>. Журнал поверх того же форматирования: уровни, источники, сменные приёмники вывода и отсечение по уровню на этапе компиляции. Цветной вывод в терминал и чтение строк из EEPROM подключаются отдельными заголовками и не занимают места, пока не нужны.

libraries.name: FmtLog
libraries.author: G-IoT <g-iot@mail.ru>
libraries.sentence: A lightweight logger for microcontrollers: levels, sources and pluggable sinks.
libraries.paragraph: Send a log line where you need it: the library writes nowhere by itself, the sink is supplied by the application, and one message can go to several at once - the serial port while debugging, the network on a working device, a memory card for post-mortem. Levels are set per source, so a chatty part can be quieted without touching the rest, and the check happens before the message is built. Critical and system levels are never suppressed. Ready-made sinks: serial port, coloured terminal output, telnet with history, and a web page fed over SSE. Both network sinks keep their own place per connection, so a client joining late sees the same depth as the first one. Pattern formatting comes from the FmtTiny library.

libraries.name: DigiCDCFast
libraries.author: Ihsan Kehribar and Digistump LLC (DigiCDC), OBJECTIVE DEVELOPMENT Software GmbH (V-USB), Marco Carnut
libraries.sentence: USB CDC serial port for the Digispark (ATtiny85) and Digispark Pro, without the throughput limits and bugs of DigisparkCDC.
libraries.paragraph: Fork of the DigisparkCDC library from the Digistump AVR core 1.7.5 with the same SerialUSB API. The original waits 5 ms after every byte written, 1 ms before every USB poll and sends a zero-length packet after every data packet, which caps output near 200 bytes/s; without them it reaches 8000 bytes/s. Also fixes receive stalls, lost data and flush(), keeps the host's line settings (baud()), and offers DigiCDCMedium.h with 2-byte packets for timing-sensitive sketches. Needs the Digistump AVR core. Tested on Linux (PC, Raspberry Pi); Windows refuses low-speed USB serial devices.

Also fixes receive stalls, lost data and flush(), keeps the host's line settings (baud()), and offers DigiCDCMedium.h with 2-byte packets for timing-sensitive sketches. libraries.name: DigiCDCFast
libraries.author: Ihsan Kehribar and Digistump LLC (DigiCDC), OBJECTIVE DEVELOPMENT Software GmbH (V-USB), Marco Carnut
libraries.sentence: USB CDC serial port for the Digispark (ATtiny85) and Digispark Pro, without the throughput limits and bugs of DigisparkCDC.
libraries.paragraph: Fork of the DigisparkCDC library from the Digistump AVR core 1.7.5 with the same SerialUSB API. The original waits 5 ms after every byte written, 1 ms before every USB poll and sends a zero-length packet after every data packet, which caps output near 200 bytes/s; without them it reaches 8000 bytes/s. Also fixes receive stalls, lost data and flush(), keeps the host's line settings (baud()), and offers DigiCDCMedium.h with 2-byte packets for timing-sensitive sketches. Since 1.1.0 about 450 bytes of flash smaller, with buffer sizes a sketch can choose and an optional hook to refuse line settings. A sketch can also borrow the USB interrupt at the end of each transaction (usbTransactionEnd), for work that cannot wait the 200 us a run of transactions takes, and answer vendor requests of its own beside the serial port (USB_CFG_VENDOR_HOOK), which is how one device can be a serial port to one program and something else to another without spending an endpoint. Needs the Digistump AVR core. Tested on Linux (PC, Raspberry Pi); Windows refuses low-speed USB serial devices.

libraries.name: DigiCDCMulti
libraries.author: Ihsan Kehribar and Digistump LLC (DigiCDC), OBJECTIVE DEVELOPMENT Software GmbH (V-USB), Marco Carnut
libraries.sentence: Two or three USB CDC serial ports (SerialUSB, SerialUSB1, SerialUSB2; /dev/ttyACM0 and up) from one Digispark (ATtiny85) or Digispark Pro.
libraries.paragraph: Fork of DigiCDCFast, with its fixes and speed and the same API on every port. Include DigiCDCDual.h for two ports, which share the device's 8000 bytes/s, or DigiCDCTriple.h for three, which share 4000 because a low-speed host only has the bandwidth for six data endpoints at 4-byte packets. A single port still moves 25 times what DigisparkCDC managed. The ports send no serial-state notifications (V-USB's transmit buffers all carry data), and pausing input when a receive buffer is full pauses every port. Buffer sizes are a sketch's to choose, down to one packet. A sketch can also borrow the USB interrupt at the end of each transaction (usbTransactionEnd) and answer vendor requests of its own beside the ports (USB_CFG_VENDOR_HOOK), both from DigiCDCFast 1.4.0. Needs the Digistump AVR core. Tested on Linux; Windows refuses low-speed USB serial devices.

libraries.name: esp-rtosLogger
libraries.author: Hamza Yesilmen <resmiyslmn@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: printf style logging that costs the caller a few microseconds: arguments are queued raw, a FreeRTOS task formats them later.
libraries.paragraph: logI("rpm=%d temp=%.2f", rpm, temp) copies the arguments into a 512 byte record and posts it to a static FreeRTOS queue. A low priority task on the core you choose formats the lines with the real snprintf and writes them to Serial, or to any sink you define, batched. Safe from interrupts. Measured 3.2 us p50 per call on an ESP32-S3 at 240 MHz from a 20 kHz loop on the other core. Runs on ESP32 (Arduino-ESP32 3.x) and nRF52 (Adafruit core).

libraries.name: esp-rtosLogger
libraries.author: Hamza Yesilmen <resmiyslmn@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: printf style logging that costs the caller about a microsecond: arguments go raw into a ring of the caller's own core, a FreeRTOS task formats them later.
libraries.paragraph: logI("rpm=%d temp=%.2f", rpm, temp) writes the raw arguments into a ring of the caller's own core, with that core's interrupts masked for the write, so no lock is ever shared between cores. A low priority task formats the lines with the real snprintf and sends them to Serial, or wherever logTo says, batched. Safe from interrupts and from any number of tasks. Measured on an ESP32-S3 under a SimpleFOC drive: 0.9 us mean, 1.4 us worst from a loop in IRAM, 0.5 us from an interrupt; 4.4 us on an nRF52840. Runs on ESP32 (Arduino-ESP32 3.x) and nRF52 (Adafruit core).

No RTOS, no heap allocation for coroutine frames, and deterministic failure behavior. It provides lazy Tasks, a fair cooperative scheduler, yield/delay timers, parent/child await, scheduler-local Event and bounded Queue, an ISR-safe ThreadSafeFlag bridge, and waitUntil.

libraries.author: Renzo Mischianti <renzo.mischianti@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Driver for InvenSense's MPU-9250 9-DOF IMU (3-axis gyroscope, 3-axis accelerometer & 3-axis magnetometer)
libraries.paragraph: The MPU-9250 is a system-in-package featuring acceleration full-scales of ±2 / ±4 / ±8 / ±16 (g), rotational full-scales of ±250 / ±500 / ±1000 / ±2000 (°/sec) and a magnetic field full scale of ±4800 µT. libraries.name: NovaHeap_Relay
libraries.author: NovaHeap Technologies
libraries.sentence: Safe, non-blocking relay control: active-LOW or active-HIGH, no click at boot, interlocks, minimum on/off times and timed pulses.
libraries.paragraph: Interlock groups keep motor forward/reverse or fan speed relays from ever being on together, with an optional dead time. libraries.name: RcLights
libraries.author: Maximilian Bauer <maximilian@bauer.pub>
libraries.sentence: Scale light controller for an RC car: three PWM channels in, six PWM light outputs out.
libraries.paragraph: Reads steering, throttle and a switch from a receiver and drives park and driving light, tail and brake light, reversing light, two turn signals and an auxiliary output. The turn signals only trigger after the steering has been centred for a moment, so cornering indicates and line corrections do not; the brake and reverse logic follows the ESC you actually have. Channel 3 is a two- or three-position switch whose positions you assign to hazards, an auxiliary output or a light switch. The decision logic is plain C with no Arduino dependency and is covered by host tests; the Arduino layer only measures pulses and writes PWM. Builds for AVR, ESP32 and STM32, and its pin capture works on all three -- on AVR it brings its own pin-change interrupts, because two external interrupt pins are one short of three channels.

libraries.name: KT_SHT40
libraries.author: Kacper Tora
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for Sensirion SHT40 I2C temperature and humidity sensors.
libraries.paragraph: Driver for Sensirion SHT40 digital relative humidity and temperature sensors. Features hardware CRC-8 data integrity checks, configurable precision modes, full on-chip pulsed heater control for de-condensation/diagnostics, 32-bit unique serial number readout, and software reset. Highly optimized for memory-constrained platforms including AVR, ESP8266, ESP32, STM32, and RP2040.

libraries.paragraph: Provides automatic ST7789 LCD setup, console wrapping and scrolling, tab handling, global printf LCD output, and scanf input from the Serial Monitor for ESP32-S3 E-Badge sketches.

libraries.name: CRSFv3
libraries.author: Maximilian Bauer <maximilian@bauer.pub>
libraries.sentence: Complete TBS CRSFv3: telemetry, RC channels, parameters, MAVLink and MSP tunnels, commands and routing.
libraries.paragraph: An Arduino wrapper over the portable c_crsf core, which also runs on ESP-IDF and STM32. Frame layer with both header forms and both CRC polynomials, the full telemetry set, 0x16/0x17/0x18 channels, the parameter protocol in both directions, MAVLink and MSP tunnels with chunking and reassembly, 0x32 Direct Commands, multi-port routing and CRSFv3 baudrate negotiation. AVR is not supported: the core needs about 3.5 KB of RAM against an ATmega328P's 2 KB. This version compiles for four architectures and passes the host test suites, but has NOT been verified against radio hardware.

libraries.name: CRSFv3
libraries.author: Maximilian Bauer <maximilian@bauer.pub>
libraries.sentence: Complete TBS CRSFv3: telemetry, RC channels, parameters, MAVLink and MSP tunnels, commands and routing.
libraries.paragraph: An Arduino wrapper over the portable c_crsf core, which also runs on ESP-IDF and STM32. Frame layer with both header forms and both CRC polynomials, the full telemetry set, 0x16/0x17/0x18 channels, the parameter protocol in both directions, MAVLink and MSP tunnels with chunking and reassembly, 0x32 Direct Commands, multi-port routing and CRSFv3 baudrate negotiation. AVR needs the compile-time switches: define CRSF_ARDUINO_MINIMAL in src/crsf_local_conf.h and a receiver or transmitter station fits an ATmega328P with room to spare, at the cost of the tunnels and the parameter protocol. Compiles for five architectures and passes the host test suites.

libraries.sentence: Cryptographically secure pairing and communication between ESP32 boards: pair through a single standard LED with the LX.25 protocol, or over ESP-NOW and LoRa.
libraries.paragraph: Beta. Two boards agree on a key with X25519, the user checks that both show the same short code (on an LED, an RGB LED or as digits), then messages are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, with replay protection. Persistent identities, up to 8 peers, safe re-pairing. Pair over one medium and talk over another: PacketLED (light), ESP-NOW, LoRa or your own. Once the chip has its own eFuse key, the saved keys are encrypted with it.

libraries.name: RangeMonitor
libraries.author: Péter Soós
libraries.sentence: Range monitor for a scalar measurement: spike filter, time-based EMA, soft limits with alarm delay, hard limits, fault detection.
libraries.paragraph: Watches any scalar quantity — temperature, humidity, pressure — against a range. A median-of-3 spike filter and a time-based EMA smooth the value; soft limits raise an alarm only after a configurable delay (tolerating defrost cycles, opened doors), hard limits raise it at once. Invalid samples become a FAULT after their own delay. Every transition is reported, every time rule uses the real time between samples, and the state machine runs on a host PC for testing and data replay. No dynamic allocation; thread-safe on ESP32 with a static FreeRTOS mutex.

libraries.paragraph: DevLab LM35 library to read temperature (0.01 C), millivolts and raw ADC counts through DDP over I2C (Device ID 0x0113).

libraries.name: TemperatureMonitor
libraries.author: Péter Soós
libraries.sentence: Monitored DS18B20 temperature channels on one 1-Wire bus: address-bound slots, persistence, non-blocking cycle, state-change events.
libraries.paragraph: Each channel binds a sensor's ROM address to its name, limits and enabled flag, stored together in one record, so readings and configuration cannot drift apart when sensors are added, removed or reordered. Discovery at start-up, automatic reconnection of missing sensors, a non-blocking measuring cycle with one broadcast conversion, and events for every state change (including MISSING and DISABLED). Changes are guarded by the expected address. Range monitoring by RangeMonitor, sensor handling by DS18B20Sensor. No dynamic allocation; host-testable.

libraries.name: AlfredoFusion
libraries.author: Alfredo Systems
libraries.sentence: IMU drivers (LSM6 family, H3LIS331DL, MMC5983MA) and VQF sensor fusion with automatic gyro bias calibration.
libraries.paragraph: Short, simple drivers for the ST LSM6 accelerometer/gyroscope family, the ST H3LIS331DL high-g accelerometer and the MEMSIC MMC5983MA magnetometer, plus the VQF orientation filter (Laidig and Seel 2023): quaternion and yaw/pitch/roll from any IMU, with gyro bias learned automatically whenever the sensor rests. Used by the Alfredo-NoU3 and SimpleMelt libraries.

libraries.name: 7Semi VL6180X
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Lightweight and efficient VL6180X Time-of-Flight distance and ambient light sensor library.
libraries.paragraph: Provides a clean, high-performance interface for the STMicroelectronics VL6180X sensor over I2C. Includes support for distance measurement, ambient light sensing, interrupts, threshold detection, GPIO configuration, ALS gain control, integration time configuration, and continuous measurement modes. Built on 7Semi BusCore for embedded efficiency and ease of use.

libraries.name: 7Semi Bus
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Universal I2C and SPI register access framework for sensor drivers.
libraries.paragraph: Hardware-independent communication layer for I2C and SPI devices. Supports 8-bit and 16-bit register addressing, 8-bit and 16-bit data transfers, endian conversion, burst read/write operations, and bit-level register access for reusable sensor driver development.

libraries.name: 7Semi INA240
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for INA240 bidirectional current sense amplifiers.
libraries.paragraph: Supports INA240A1, INA240A2 and INA240A3 current sense amplifiers with bidirectional current measurement, offset calibration, ADC averaging, shunt voltage calculation and current calculation.

libraries.name: 7Semi VL53L1X
libraries.author: 7Semi <info@7semi.com>
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for VL53L1X time-of-flight distance sensor (ToF).
libraries.paragraph: Lightweight driver for VL53L1X ToF sensor with default configuration, range presets (SHORT/MEDIUM/LONG), timing budget control, blocking read API, interrupt handling, and calibration support via I2C (TwoWire).

libraries.name: 7Semi MCP4725
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Arduino Library for the 7semi MCP4725 12-bit I2C DAC Module.
libraries.paragraph: Supports 12-bit analog output using MCP4725 over I2C. Features fast mode (no EEPROM write), configurable I2C speed, and support for multiple wire ports.

libraries.name: 7Semi AS7343
libraries.author: 7Semi <info@7semi.com>
libraries.sentence: Multi-channel spectral sensor driver for AS7343.
libraries.paragraph: Flexible I2C driver for the ams OSRAM AS7343 spectral sensor. Supports multi-channel light sensing, SMUX configuration (6/12/18 channels), gain control, integration time adjustment, FIFO streaming, interrupt handling, flicker detection, LED control, and threshold-based alerts.

libraries.name: 7Semi AS7343
libraries.author: Supratik Das
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for the 7Semi AS7343 14 channel multi-spectral sensor.
libraries.paragraph: Reads 12 spectral channels and VIS and NIR data, controls the LED, and detects flicker.

libraries.name: 7Semi HDC302x
libraries.author: 7Semi <info@7semi.com>
libraries.sentence: High-accuracy temperature and humidity sensor driver for HDC302x.
libraries.paragraph: Flexible I2C driver for the Texas Instruments HDC302x temperature and humidity sensor. Supports single-shot and continuous measurements, configurable output data rate (ODR), power modes, heater control, alert thresholds with hysteresis, and offset calibration.

libraries.name: 7Semi SHT2x
libraries.author: 7Semi <info@7semi.com>
libraries.sentence: Driver for Sensirion SHT2x Temperature and Humidity Sensor with CRC check and flexible I2C pin configuration.
libraries.paragraph: Provides temperature (°C) and humidity (%RH) readings with CRC validation, soft reset, heater control, OTP reload, battery flag, resolution selection, and electronic serial number readout. Compatible with ESP32, ESP8266, and AVR boards.

libraries.name: 7Semi MCP4728
libraries.author: 7Semi
libraries.sentence: Arduino library for the MCP4728 4-channel 12-bit DAC over I2C.
libraries.paragraph: Supports fast write, multi write, sequential write with optional EEPROM, general call update, and full DAC/EERPOM readback functionality.

libraries.name: 7Semi MCP9808
libraries.author: 7Semi <info@7semi.com>
libraries.sentence: High-accuracy digital temperature sensor driver for MCP9808.
libraries.paragraph: Flexible I2C driver for the Microchip MCP9808 temperature sensor. Supports temperature measurement, alert thresholds (upper, lower, critical), hysteresis control, power modes, and configurable resolution.

libraries.name: 7Semi DS2482
libraries.author: 7Semi <info@7semi.com>
libraries.sentence: I2C to 1-Wire bridge driver for DS2482.
libraries.paragraph: Lightweight and reliable Arduino driver for Maxim DS2482 I2C to 1-Wire bridge. Supports 1-Wire reset, read/write operations, ROM search, and DS18B20 temperature sensors. Designed for multi-device 1-Wire networks with efficient bus handling.

libraries.paragraph: A feature-rich library designed for classroom AI and IoT projects, supporting Teachable Machine Webapp via MQTT.

libraries.name: PIDNonBlocking
libraries.author: George Arun
libraries.sentence: Non-blocking PID controller that runs on its own sample period from the main loop.
libraries.paragraph: Plain C core: derivative on measurement, low-pass filtered derivative, trapezoidal integral, anti-windup. PIDController_Run() never waits: it computes only when the sample period has elapsed on millis(), passes the true elapsed time as dt, stays phase-locked to the sample grid and holds its output in between. Sample periods from 1 ms to minutes.

libraries.name: JoystickUtilities
libraries.author: Christoph Streit <christoph.streit@gmail.com>
libraries.sentence: Read, calibrate and store analog thumb sticks, with direction keys for menus.
libraries.paragraph: Maps each axis to -1000..1000 with a dead zone, averaging and optional inversion. Provides the building blocks of a calibration - averaging the resting position, recording the travel while the stick is swept, checking the result per axis - and leaves the procedure (Serial prompts, a display, buttons) to the sketch. Direction keys with auto-repeat turn a stick into up/down/left/right events. Stores calibrations with Preferences on ESP32. Reads physical joysticks; it does not emulate a USB game controller.
